READ LIVE 2026-09-21 with get_metadata - the interior this row has never had, the last passes having inferred it from its Easy sibling - and the inference was WRONG on the two things that matter. 954 x 621. The shell is as expected and as recorded: board 9411:7956 453x453 at (250.5,50), legend 9411:7964 340x50 at (307,553) on the 58 pitch, column 9442:16756 66x356 at (853,99) with its inner row hidden. THE SIBLING DOES NOT PREDICT THE CONTENT: this cut's legend prints 0.2x / 0.5x / 2.5x / 3.6x / 8.8x / 63x where Easy 9411:7933 prints 0.5x / 0.8x / 1.2x / 1.5x / 2.7x / 8.5x, and its board rings are a different set too - 453 / 405.41595 / 386.38232 / 291.21426 / 160.33145 with a 23.79202 bull, i.e. fractions 1.0 / 0.894958 / 0.852941 / 0.642857 / 0.353933 / 0.052521 against Easy's 1.0 / 0.894958 / 0.852941 / 0.747899 / 0.411764 / 0.096639. The outer two rims are shared and everything inside them shrinks. So THE FRAME EXPRESSES DIFFICULTY AS A SMALLER TARGET PAYING MORE, while the rail expresses it as a lower per-ring PROBABILITY across one fixed multiplier set and one fixed geometry (DIFFICULTY_WEIGHTS; dartsBoardGeometry.ts pins the radii to the rail's DARTS_RINGS and says why). Two designs of one product idea, and the standing note that the frame prints six values the rail never paid was reading one of three boards. NOTHING BUILT ON THAT PATH and nothing may be: it is a paytable and a ring boundary, both money. The docblock in dartsBoardGeometry.ts records the Easy fractions only and is now a third of the picture - a row for the next pass rather than an edit, since that file is a rail oracle. No browser ran.

That is what ba27a3c3 built, citing this node; this is the first independent read of it and every number closes: pl-[6.2148%] = 7/112.6332, pr-[6.777%] = 7.6332/112.6332, top 6.0518% = 6.8164/112.6332 settled and 4.2761% = 4.8164/112.6332 armed. THE ONE DIVERGENCE IS THE ROW'S PLACEMENT, AND IT IS NOW CORROBORATED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: both cuts put the row at (181, 217.1836) to four decimals. Neither coordinate is derived - centring gives x = 179.417, so the row is positioned as if it were 592 wide and is 1.58 out, and the y is exact centring inside a 547-tall region whose floor matches nothing either board draws, the footer opening at 511 and the 10215 strip at 556. The desktop board takes its height from the panel, so a literal 217 breaks at every other height. Two boards agreeing is not a rule: recorded, not built. No browser ran.

READ LIVE 2026-09-21 with get_metadata, OUT OF SLICE and taken deliberately: it is the third witness the difficulty finding needed, because with two boards a per-difficulty paytable is still indistinguishable from one board's typo. 954 x 621, and the SHELL is its siblings' to the pixel - board 9411:7978 453x453 at (250.5,50), legend 9411:7986 340x50 at (307,553) with six 50x50 chips on the 58 pitch, throw column 9442:16771 66x356 at (853,99) with its inner row hidden, which is the third board to reserve that gutter and the third confirmation of a3f80572. ★★ THE THREE VISIBLE LEGENDS ARE THREE DIFFERENT PAYTABLES. Hard prints 0.1x / 0.5x / 4.8x / 9.6x / 42x / 500x; Medium 9411-7955 prints 0.2x / 0.5x / 2.5x / 3.6x / 8.8x / 63x; Easy 9411-7933 prints 0.5x / 0.8x / 1.2x / 1.5x / 2.7x / 8.5x - a top chip running 8.5x, 63x, 500x. ★ AND THAT CORRECTS THIS NODE'S OWN EARLIER VERDICT, which is why the read was worth a seat slot: the closed line on this key reads 'same hidden duplicate six-value group as 9411-7955', and the two groups are NOT the same object. The hidden group here is inside the THROW COLUMN (9442:16772, hidden=true) and prints 0.5x / 8.5x / 1.5x / 0.8x / 1.2x / 2.7x, which is Easy's set shuffled and is the un-updated duplication that pass correctly spotted. The 500x is not in it. It is in Frame 1000004121, the board's own VISIBLE legend, in the same node role at the same (307,553) on which Easy's and Medium's were read. THE RAIL DOES THE OPPOSITE, AND IN ONE PLACE: supabase/functions/_shared/paytables.ts:113-136 holds ONE multiplier set for all three difficulties (Miss 0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.65, 1.55, 3, Bullseye 8) on ONE geometry (radii 52 / 42 / 33 / 24 / 15 / 6 out of 65) and expresses difficulty ONLY as DARTS_PROBABILITY_WEIGHTS - easy [36,6,10,19,16,10,3] 95.35%, normal [49,7,8,11,11,9,5] 95.00%, hard [57,7,4,8,10,8,6] 95.30%. The frame varies the PRIZE; the rail varies the CHANCE and lands all three RTPs inside 0.35 of a point. THE DRAWN RINGS FOLLOW THE LEGEND RATHER THAN THE RAIL, AND THEY ARE NOT EVEN A RAMP: this cut nests 453 / 405.41595 / 386.38239 / 291.21426 / 196.04622 and carries NO bullseye node at all - five discs under six chips - where Easy nests to a 0.096639 bull and Medium to a 0.052521 one. Its innermost disc is 0.432781 of the board against Medium's 0.353933, i.e. Hard draws the LARGER target and prints the larger multiplier. Whatever the three boards encode, it is not one rule, so no geometry can be derived from them either. NOTHING BUILT AND NOTHING MAY BE: a multiplier and a ring boundary are both money. The shipped page keeps ONE legend at the rail's six values with the caption that difficulty changes how often each ring lands rather than what it pays, and that stays until Casey rules. FOR CASEY, and it is ONE decision over all three boards rather than three. THE CLIENT COPY IS IN SYNC AND WAS ALREADY BOUND: DartsGame.tsx equals the rail array for array, and dartsBoardGeometry.test.ts parses both out of their two source files and fails on any difference. Its docblock claimed nothing bound them, which had stood long enough to read as a standing warning to be careful by hand; corrected at skai-gaming 70b9b637, along with a Source-of-truth pointer aimed at points-game/index.ts, which re-exports rather than declares. ★ AND THE SAME LOOK FOUND THE COPY THAT REALLY IS UNGUARDED: supabase/functions/game-settlement/index.ts:4265-4284 declares its OWN DARTS_RINGS and DARTS_PROBABILITY_WEIGHTS rather than importing the shared ones, and that is the copy deciding what a player is paid. Four copies of these numbers exist and all four agree at HEAD, so this is a drift surface rather than a live defect - but a change to the shared table that missed it would pay two different games of darts. supabase/ is fenced, so it is this row and not an edit. No browser ran.

NOT RE-READ IN FIGMA THIS PASS AND SAID SO: the 2026-09-20 live get_metadata reading of all three children stands, and this wave's 00:2x hash check found all 51 pages unchanged, so the board this row was measured against is the board the catalog counts. What this pass did was read CoinflipWinCard.tsx at HEAD against that reading, element by element, and every number closes. Card 10215:6237 159 x 125: h-[125px] w-[159px], radius 8 as a literal because this codebase's rounded-lg is 12. Padding: the frame draws 32 with its 4px stroke aligned INSIDE, and CSS pads after the border, so border-4 with p-[28px] is the same 32 from the outer edge - which is what puts the stack's corner on 10215:6238's (32,32) and leaves it the 95 x 61 that node is drawn at. Stack rows on the frame's 8 seam: multiplier Manrope Bold 18 on a 25 line box, a 55 x 2 rule, then the payout line - 25 + 8 + 2 + 8 + 18 = 61, exact. Payout Mulish Bold 14 on 18. Tracking -0.04em is -0.72 at 18 and -0.56 at 14, both the frame's. Colours come through coinflipTheme rather than as literals: face COINFLIP.inset, border COINFLIP.win, and the hard 0 4px 0 shadow with no blur that the frame draws. ★ THE ONE DIVERGENCE IS THE CURRENCY BADGE, AND IT IS DECIDED BY A STANDING RULE RATHER THAN OPEN: the frame draws one fixed blue USDC-style disc, 16 x 16 at x=79 inside the 95-wide row 3. Coinflip settles in POINTS, SKAI or sUSD, so one hardcoded glyph would mislabel two rails out of three on the single surface where the unit is a money claim and not decoration. The badge carries the ACTIVE rail's symbol instead, resolved by the caller through the same tokenDisplaySymbol the balance row and the result line already use, and row 3's width therefore follows the symbol rather than landing on 95. Building the frame's disc would be changing a RAIL LABEL to match a design, which the wave's rules forbid outright, so this is a rule-decided call and the row closes on it. Casey can override; it is one line in the report as a choice. NODE-NAME TRAPS HOLD AND ARE BUILT TO THE RENDER: the coin layer is named `Tails Loss` on both win boards and renders green, and the payout text node is named `2.340195` while the string it draws is `300.50303`. The component takes both as formatted props from the settlement response and re-derives no payout, because the rails floor and a float product does not. The board's other two children were measured on 09-20 and are unchanged here: strip 10215:6195 854 x 35 at (50,556) over an 838 x 15 row, twenty slots on a 43.3158 pitch with six filled and fourteen empty - identical to its first beat 10215-5078, which is the evidence the two frames are one round a moment apart - and coin 10215:6229 260 x 260 at (347,181) as a stacked annulus at 260 / 255 / 250. 1440 only: this frame draws no 768 or 375 cut. No browser ran.
